newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index down 0.7 pct at 285.94.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index down 0.7 pct at 285.94.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars, fell 0.7 percent to 285.94 at midsession on Monday.
Latin America lost 0.5 percent day-on-day, slipping to 513.75; Asia was down 0.6 percent at 248.50, and Europe, Middle East and Africa shed 1.4 percent, falling to 129.04.
The IFC composite index touched a 1996 high of 308.77 on July 4, up from the year's 275.79 low, recorded on January 1.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index, also denominated in dollars, was down 0.68 percent day-on-day at 155.78 at 1445 GMT.
The year's high was 165.948, reached on July 3. It touched the year's 148.85 low on January 2.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index was down 0.60 percent at 462.899, calculated after the close of trade on Friday.
It touched a 1996 high of 505.452 on July 4. The year's 458.369 low was recorded on January 1.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns from some 20 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns from 22 emerging market nations. Changes are reported with one day's lag at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index, its returns calculated in dollar terms, shed 0.02 percent to 123.69 by the start of trade on Monday.
By region, Latin America was down 0.09 percent at 100.54, Asia was flat at 130.99 and East Europe was down 0.23 at 162.33. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
